title: spermacoce brachysepala
intro: Spermacoce brachysepala, commonly known as Wild Jasmine, is a plant species in the Rubiaceae family. It is traditionally used in folk medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which can help to alleviate symptoms of fever, cough, and respiratory issues. The bioactive constituents of Wild Jasmine include alkaloids, flavonoids, and saponins, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, such as sedative, anti-anxiety, and antispasmodic effects. The plant is also valued for its potential to reduce inflammation and improve sleep quality, making it a popular remedy in traditional medicine.
